source.title: Some Open Problems in Computational Geometry

accepted.question_text: Given a set P of n stochastic points in R^d, where each point p in P exists independently with input probability pi(p) in (0,1], let R be the resulting random subset and let box(R) be the smallest axis-aligned box containing R. The expected volume of box(R) is known to be computable in O(n log n) time for d = 2 and in O(n^{d-1} log n) time for each fixed d >= 3, while exact computation is #P-hard when d is unbounded and d = Theta(n). Determine the parameterized complexity as a function of d: is the decision version W[1]-hard, or is it fixed-parameter tractable in d? Also find efficient approximation schemes whose dependence on d is small.

Given n unit disks, or n axis-parallel unit squares, in the plane, define the intersection graph with one vertex for each geometric object and an edge between two distinct objects exactly when they intersect. Can a maximum matching in this geometric intersection graph be computed in near-linear time?
accepted.context_brief: Maximum matching in unit disk or square graphs

accepted.question_text: Given a red family and a blue family of unit disks, or of axis-parallel unit squares, in the plane, form the bipartite intersection graph whose vertices are all objects and whose edges connect only intersecting red-blue pairs. Can a maximum matching in this bipartite geometric intersection graph be found in near-linear time?
accepted.context_brief: Bipartite matching in bichromatic unit disk or square graphs

accepted.question_text: Given a finite family D of unit disks in the plane and two points s and t not covered by any disk, define the annular-domain barrier-resilience problem as finding an s-t curve in the plane that touches as few disks of D as possible, equivalently removing as few disks as possible so that an s-t curve avoids all remaining disks. Determine the computational complexity of this problem for disks or unit disks in the annular domain: is there a polynomial-time algorithm, or is the problem NP-hard?

In the rectangular-domain shrinking-barrier problem for unit disks, the point s lies above all disks, the point t lies below all disks, paths are restricted to a vertical slab containing s and t, and each disk may be shrunk by an individually chosen amount. The objective is to minimize the total amount of shrinking required to allow an s-t path that avoids the shrunk disks. Although an approximation scheme is known for this rectangular-domain problem, determine whether the exact optimization problem is NP-hard, and settle its computational complexity.

needs_review.question_text_raw: In both cases, bipartite or not bipartite, recognizing whether the (bipartite) intersection graph has a maximum matching, possibly without explicitly constructing it, seems an interesting challenge.
